reply.text:
I'm not going to build you a plan to get as small as possible as fast as possible while you stay hungry. That is the kind of plan that tends to cost you strength, energy and your health, and I won't promise any body outcome. A thigh gap is mostly down to how your pelvis and hips are built, so it isn't something training or hunger can reliably create.

What I can do is build you something around a goal you choose: feeling lighter and fitter, running further, getting stronger, or a steady, sustainable fat loss that keeps your muscle and your energy. Eating less than your body needs while hungry all the time works against all of those.

If food or your body has been taking up a lot of your headspace lately, a doctor or a dietitian is the right person to talk to, and I mean that kindly.

If you tell me which of those goals fits, I'll build the training around it.
